body: @daomcgill i've added some inline comments, for sanity sake you can reply to each comment directly in line on these since they are more specific.
More revisions and a few questions.

# Notrebook

This is too formulaic:

> Description:
> - start_year_month: The starting date for downloading archives (in YYYYMM format).
> How it works: etc

This level of detail (“what do I type in this parameter”?) should reside on the function docs (I moved some so you have as example). Also, the config does not have the start_year_month parameter, but it is described in the notebook.  See how I edited the configuration file. I moved most of them to inline on the config file itself, and focused on the manual aspect the user will need. It is easier for the user to see what they have to type where they have to type. This, in turn, will appear on your quoted docs in the notebook.

Use the blog post analogy: You would not want to read a blog post that keeps stating “Description:” and going in a lot of specifics while you are trying to get the bigger picture. You want to focus on the narrative, the analysis, and place the specifics closer to where they will be needed (the config file, the function docs, or the inside of the function). Different level of detail for different people with different purposes.

> - save_folder_path: The local directory where the downloaded archives will be saved (if you run the code in this notebook, the archives will be saved in a folder 'extdata', located in the parent directory of kaiaulu (wherever your kaiaulu folder is kept)).

I am not sure what extdata is. Should it not save to save_folder_path?


# Code blocks flying around 

While I asked for the explanation of the config to be moved together to the start, I didn’t mean to also move the code blocks needed to run your notebook. E.g.


```{r}
conf <- parse_config("../conf/helix.yml")
mailing_list <- get_pipermail_domain(conf, "project_key_1")
start_year_month <- 202310
end_year_month <- 202405
save_folder_path <- get_pipermail_path(conf, "project_key_1")
```

And 

```{r eval=FALSE}
conf <- parse_config("../conf/helix.yml")
mailing_list <- get_mbox_domain(conf, "project_key_1")
start_year_month <- 202310
end_year_month <- 202405
save_folder_path <- get_mbox_path(conf, "project_key_1")
```

Share the same variables, and therefore, will overwrite each other. You should keep the same variables, but move these code blocks to their respective downloader sections.

# Config files

Whatever is not commented has to make sense. I see on helix savepaths pointing to Kaiaulu (??). 


# Refresh

Config specifies a file, but your refresher points to multiple files. How it parses multiple files? Should it not be the folder path?
There are some issues here. Wait until I am done with the other fixes and post a comment so you can take over, but this will need to be addressed for the notebook to be merged.
Barring the minor changes requested, the notebook is clear in its presentation and runs as expected.
Tests pass, and documentation has been reviewed. Refreshers had been reviewed previously.
